resolved_parts_audit.policy: Representative source-positive chamber branch within the named Wind Symphony field, not a universal wind-symphony lineup. Ohio State’s whole separately identified Mozart overture adaptation retains Harmonie pairs of oboes, clarinets, horns and bassoons and explicitly adds flute and double bass. All six instrument families are retained; four pairs are aggregated by family cards, not falsely six people. No other pieces’ piano, banjo or percussion are imported, and no actual performer assignments are guessed. Authored modern concert apparatus: American-scrape modern grenadilla oboe/Loree school, grenadilla A clarinet/medium reed/tongued articulation, full yellow-brass horn, Heckel maple/cane orchestral bassoon, silver C flute/Powell school/classical embouchure, steel-strung bowed double bass. These are editable source-compatible choices, not assertions of actual maker, transposition, string material or historical period instruments. Shared wind articulation is continuous legato, compatible with ensemble phrasing; clarinet local tonguing remains an articulation dimension, not perpetual detached playing. Shoebox concert listening acoustics authored rather than measured Weigel geometry. Broad common-practice parent applies to this Mozart chamber realization, not a claim the whole field excludes contemporary composition. No global tuning precision is asserted.
